Repayment secured through post-dated cheques (PDCs), as per the lender's structure

caseStudies.headline: ₹2.4 crore sanctioned — no salary slip, no problem
caseStudies.clientProfile: A self-employed architect running an established design practice in Thane, with strong monthly billings but no salary slip and income that varies year to year.
caseStudies.challenge: Two banks rejected the application at the initial screening stage, citing "income not verifiable" — a common outcome for self-employed applicants whose income doesn't fit a standard salaried-income template.
caseStudies.structuring: GCS reviewed 18 months of banking activity and client-billing records alongside the applicant's ITRs, and matched the profile with a lender whose underwriting norms specifically accommodate self-employed and professional income assessed on banking turnover rather than salary slips.
caseStudies.outcome: ₹2.4 crore home loan sanctioned by the matched lender, against the client's target property in Thane.

caseStudies.category: Loan Against Property · Balance Transfer + Top-Up
caseStudies.headline: ₹2.6 crore unlocked — one property, a lower rate, fresh capital to expand
caseStudies.clientProfile: A growing trading business owner in Mumbai carrying an existing Loan Against Property from another lender at a rate that had crept up over three years, wanting extra funds to expand inventory.
caseStudies.challenge: The client's existing lender had no incentive to reduce the rate on a running facility, and a fresh application elsewhere would have meant re-starting the entire property and income verification process from scratch.
caseStudies.structuring: GCS reviewed the existing loan's outstanding principal, tenure and current rate, and identified a lender offering a materially better rate for a balance transfer plus an additional top-up sized to the client's business requirement — combining both into a single new facility.
caseStudies.outcome: ₹2.6 crore facility approved (existing ₹1.8 crore transferred + ₹80 lakh fresh top-up), with a lower monthly EMI than the client's original loan despite the additional funds.

caseStudies.category: Home Loan Balance Transfer · Existing Customer Loan Review
caseStudies.headline: ₹4,200 shaved off every EMI — one question nobody had asked in 5 years
caseStudies.clientProfile: A salaried couple in Mumbai, five years into a home loan taken with their salary-account bank at the time, who had never checked whether a better rate was available elsewhere.
caseStudies.challenge: The couple weren't aware their current rate had fallen behind what new-to-bank customers were being offered elsewhere for a similar profile — a common blind spot, since most borrowers only revisit a home loan when something goes wrong.
caseStudies.structuring: GCS ran a loan review — outstanding principal, remaining tenure, current rate and applicable transfer costs — and compared this against balance-transfer offers from lenders in its network for the client's current profile.
caseStudies.outcome: Loan transferred to a new lender at a lower rate, reducing the monthly EMI by roughly ₹4,200 for the remaining tenure, with no change to the loan amount or the property.

caseStudies.headline: ₹62 lakh funded — zero collateral, one government guarantee
caseStudies.clientProfile: A growing manufacturing unit in Navi Mumbai, two years into operations, with consistent GST filings and healthy banking turnover, but no owned commercial or residential property to offer as collateral.
caseStudies.challenge: Most business-loan lenders wanted collateral given the business's short operating history, effectively ruling out standard secured business loan routes for the funding the business needed.
caseStudies.structuring: GCS structured the application under the CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises) route, where a government-backed guarantee substitutes for physical collateral, and matched the client with a lender empanelled for CGTMSE-backed lending.
caseStudies.outcome: ₹62 lakh collateral-free business loan sanctioned under the CGTMSE scheme.

caseStudies.headline: ₹55 lakh sanctioned — on banking strength, not the ITR
caseStudies.clientProfile: An established trading firm in Mumbai, three years in business, with strong monthly banking credits but an ITR that understated real turnover — common for cash-heavy trading businesses.
caseStudies.challenge: Standard business-loan underwriting leans heavily on ITR-declared income, and an ITR-only assessment would have supported a much smaller loan than the business could actually service.
caseStudies.structuring: GCS built the case around 12 months of banking turnover and GST filings rather than ITR alone, and matched the profile with a lender whose credit policy weighs banking strength for trading businesses.
caseStudies.outcome: ₹55 lakh unsecured business loan sanctioned — nearly double what an ITR-only assessment would have supported.

caseStudies.headline: ₹68 lakh working capital — released before the order was lost
caseStudies.clientProfile: A garment exporter in Navi Mumbai with a strong seasonal order book, but cash tied up in receivables right when a large new order needed raw-material payment upfront.
caseStudies.challenge: The business's own cash was locked in 60-90 day receivables, and the new order's supplier wanted advance payment — a timing mismatch that had nothing to do with the business's underlying health.
caseStudies.structuring: GCS structured a cash credit facility sized to the business's stock and receivables cycle, rather than a fixed-term loan that wouldn't flex with the seasonal pattern.
caseStudies.outcome: ₹68 lakh working capital limit sanctioned, drawn against as needed rather than disbursed as a lump sum.

caseStudies.headline: ₹24 lakh, disbursed in days — when a medical bill couldn't wait
caseStudies.clientProfile: A senior salaried IT professional in Pune with a clean credit history, strong take-home pay and stable employment, needing funds quickly for a major family medical emergency.
caseStudies.challenge: Time was the constraint, not eligibility — the client needed funds within days, and going lender-by-lender to compare processing timelines would have cost valuable time.
caseStudies.structuring: Given the client's clean profile, GCS routed the application directly to a lender known for minimal documentation and fast turnaround for salaried applicants with strong credit scores.
caseStudies.outcome: ₹24 lakh personal loan sanctioned and disbursed within a few working days of application.

caseStudies.headline: ₹22 lakh for a degree abroad — one lender said no, structuring said yes
caseStudies.clientProfile: A student from Pune admitted to a postgraduate professional course abroad, whose parents' individual income wasn't, on its own, sufficient to meet a single lender's income criteria for the full loan amount.
caseStudies.challenge: The family's instinct was to apply with just one parent as co-applicant against their salary alone, which fell short of what most lenders wanted to see for a loan of this size.
caseStudies.structuring: GCS reviewed the combined household income and identified a lender willing to consider both parents as joint co-applicants, alongside the standard admission and cost documentation for the course.
caseStudies.outcome: ₹22 lakh education loan sanctioned, covering tuition and living costs for the course.

caseStudies.headline: 100% on-road funding — a first car, zero down payment
caseStudies.clientProfile: A first-time car buyer in Pune, two years into a salaried role, wanting to avoid a large down payment on a new hatchback.
caseStudies.challenge: Most lenders cap funding at 85-90% of the on-road price for a first-time borrower with limited credit history, leaving a down payment gap the client hadn't budgeted for.
caseStudies.structuring: GCS matched the client with a lender offering on-road funding — covering registration and insurance, not just the ex-showroom price — for well-qualified salaried applicants.
caseStudies.outcome: 100% on-road funding approved, with no down payment required at delivery.

income-tax-return-filing.title: Income Tax Return (ITR) Filing
income-tax-return-filing.summary: Income Tax Return (ITR) filing is the process of reporting your income, deductions and taxes to the Income Tax Department. We help salaried people, professionals, business owners and firms prepare and file the right return for their income.
income-tax-return-filing.whoNeedsIt: Salaried employees, self-employed people, freelancers, business owners, firms, and anyone with rental, interest, investment or capital gains income. Filing requirements depend on your income, transactions and the Income Tax rules that apply.
process: Share your income details and documents
Review and preparation, including selecting the right ITR form
Your confirmation of the return before filing
ITR filing with the Income Tax Department
Filing acknowledgement shared for your records

tax-planning-advisory.title: Tax Planning & Advisory
tax-planning-advisory.summary: Guidance on deductions, exemptions, advance tax and tax-efficient structuring based on your income profile. We look at your full financial picture, not just the current year's filing, before recommending a plan.
tax-planning-advisory.whoNeedsIt: Individuals and businesses wanting to plan ahead rather than react at filing time. Particularly useful if your income has changed recently — a new job, a bonus, a property sale, or a new business.
process: Review of current income, investments and tax position
Applicable deductions and structuring options discussed
A practical plan for the year, including advance-tax dates where relevant

tds-return-filing.title: TDS Return Filing
tds-return-filing.summary: TDS compliance and quarterly return filing for salary, commission, rent, professional fees and other applicable payments. We reconcile challans against deductions before filing, so mismatches don't surface later as notices.
tds-return-filing.whoNeedsIt: Businesses and individuals required to deduct and report TDS on payments they make. Also useful if you've received a TDS mismatch notice and need help correcting a prior filing.
process: Deduction details for the quarter collected and reviewed
Return prepared and challans reconciled
Filed within the applicable due date, with Form 16/16A support
documents: Deduction and payment records for the quarter

tds-property-sale-26qb.title: TDS on Property Sale — Form 26QB
tds-property-sale-26qb.summary: Assistance with the applicable TDS compliance when buying a property above the notified threshold, including Form 26QB filing. We also help generate Form 16B for the seller once the deposit is confirmed.
tds-property-sale-26qb.whoNeedsIt: Buyers and sellers in a property transaction where TDS on the sale consideration applies. This typically comes up on transactions above ₹50 lakh, where the buyer must deduct and deposit TDS before registration.
process: Transaction details and applicability reviewed
Form 26QB prepared and TDS deposited
Form 16B generated for the seller

gst-registration.title: GST Registration
gst-registration.summary: New GST registration support, including document preparation and application follow-up. We track the application through the portal until the GSTIN is issued, resolving any department queries along the way.
gst-registration.whoNeedsIt: Businesses crossing the GST threshold, or those who need GST registration voluntarily. Also relevant if you're expanding into e-commerce or inter-state supply, where registration is mandatory regardless of turnover.
process: Business details and documents reviewed for eligibility
Application prepared and submitted on the GST portal
Follow-up on queries until registration is granted
documents: Business proof (registration certificate, partnership deed, etc.)

gst-return-filing.title: GST Return Filing & Compliance
gst-return-filing.summary: Monthly/quarterly GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B filing along with ongoing GST compliance support. We reconcile sales and purchase data each cycle so your returns match your books and your GSTR-2B.
gst-return-filing.whoNeedsIt: GST-registered businesses that need regular, on-time return filing. Suited to businesses that would rather hand off the monthly compliance grind than track due dates themselves.
process: Sales and purchase data collected for the period
Returns prepared and shared for review
Filed within the due date each cycle
documents: Bank statements, if required for reconciliation

gst-reconciliation-notice-support.title: GST Reconciliation & Notice Support
gst-reconciliation-notice-support.summary: GSTR-2B/books reconciliation and professional assistance in responding to applicable GST notices. We identify exactly where the mismatch originates before drafting any response to the department.
gst-reconciliation-notice-support.whoNeedsIt: Businesses with mismatches between books and GST returns, or who've received a GST notice. Also useful ahead of an annual return or audit, to clear up discrepancies before they get flagged.
process: Books and GST returns reconciled to identify gaps
Root cause reviewed and corrective filing planned
Notice, if any, reviewed and a response prepared

accounting-bookkeeping.title: Accounting & Bookkeeping
accounting-bookkeeping.summary: Monthly bookkeeping, ledger maintenance, bank reconciliation and financial statement preparation. Your books stay current through the year, so tax filing and audit season don't turn into a scramble.
accounting-bookkeeping.whoNeedsIt: Businesses and professionals who want their books maintained on an ongoing basis. A good fit if you currently rely on scattered spreadsheets or an in-house team stretched too thin to keep up.
process: Transaction data and bank statements shared each month
Books updated and reconciled
Financial statements shared periodically

tax-audit-support.title: Tax Audit Support
tax-audit-support.summary: Support for tax audit and GST-related audit/compliance requirements, for taxpayers to whom audit applies. We work through the applicable checklist and reconcile records well before the filing deadline.
tax-audit-support.whoNeedsIt: Businesses and professionals whose turnover or profile brings them under applicable audit requirements. Also useful if this is your first year crossing the audit threshold and you're unsure what's expected.
process: Applicability of audit reviewed against your turnover/profile
Books and records reviewed and reconciled
Audit report prepared and filed within the due date
documents: Prior year's audit report, if applicable

company-llp-registration.title: Company & LLP Registration
company-llp-registration.summary: Incorporation support for Private Limited Companies and LLPs, including the applicable MCA documentation. We coordinate the DSC, DIN, name approval and incorporation filing as one continuous process.
company-llp-registration.whoNeedsIt: Founders setting up a new company or LLP, or converting from a proprietorship/partnership. Also relevant if you're bringing in a co-founder or investor and need a formal corporate structure in place.
process: Structure, name and documentation requirements discussed
DSC, DIN and incorporation forms prepared and filed with MCA
Certificate of Incorporation, PAN and TAN obtained

msme-udyam-registration.title: MSME / Udyam Registration
msme-udyam-registration.summary: Udyam registration assistance for eligible micro, small and medium enterprises. Getting registered typically unlocks priority-sector lending, government tenders and other MSME-specific benefits.
msme-udyam-registration.whoNeedsIt: Proprietorships, partnerships and companies eligible for MSME classification. Especially useful before applying for a business loan, since several lenders ask for Udyam registration upfront.
process: Business and investment/turnover details reviewed
Udyam application filed against your PAN
Udyam certificate shared once generated
documents: Bank account and GST details, if applicable

shop-act-fssai-registration.title: Shop Act (Gumasta) & FSSAI Registration
shop-act-fssai-registration.summary: Maharashtra Shop & Establishment (Gumasta) registration, and FSSAI registration/licensing for eligible food businesses. We identify which registration actually applies to your setup before filing anything.
shop-act-fssai-registration.whoNeedsIt: Businesses operating a physical establishment in Maharashtra, or those dealing in food products. Also relevant when opening a new outlet, since Gumasta registration is typically required per location.
process: Applicable registration(s) identified for your business
Application prepared with the required premises/business documents
Registration/licence obtained and shared with you

pan-tan-dsc-services.title: PAN, TAN & DSC Services
pan-tan-dsc-services.summary: Application assistance for PAN, TAN and Digital Signature Certificates for individuals and businesses. We also help with corrections — a misspelled name or an outdated address — on an existing PAN.
pan-tan-dsc-services.whoNeedsIt: New businesses, or anyone needing a fresh PAN/TAN/DSC or a correction to an existing one. A DSC in particular is usually a prerequisite before any MCA or GST filing can be submitted.
process: Requirement and applicant details confirmed
Application prepared and submitted with supporting documents
PAN/TAN/DSC shared with you once issued
documents: Business registration proof, for TAN/DSC in a company or firm's name

property-title-verification.title: Property Title Verification & Due Diligence
property-title-verification.summary: Review of ownership documents, title chain, encumbrances and approvals before a property purchase. We flag anything that could complicate the sale — a pending litigation, an unclear share, or a missing approval — before you commit funds.
property-title-verification.whoNeedsIt: Buyers wanting a professional check on a property's title and documentation before committing. Especially important for resale flats, ancestral property, or anything without a clean, recent chain of ownership.
process: Property and seller documents collected
Title chain, encumbrances and approvals reviewed
Written observations shared with you

sale-agreement-sale-deed.title: Sale Agreement & Sale Deed Drafting
sale-agreement-sale-deed.summary: Drafting and registration assistance for sale agreements and sale deeds in a property transaction. We coordinate stamp duty payment and the registration appointment so the transaction closes cleanly.
sale-agreement-sale-deed.whoNeedsIt: Buyers and sellers finalising a property purchase or sale. Also useful for structuring a phased payment schedule between the agreement and the final sale deed.
process: Transaction terms and party details confirmed
Agreement/deed drafted for both parties' review
Stamp duty coordination and registration assistance

gift-release-deed.title: Gift Deed & Release Deed Documentation
gift-release-deed.summary: Drafting assistance for gift deeds and release/relinquishment deeds for family property transfers. Both documents are drafted to withstand scrutiny later, with the right stamp duty and registration handled from the start.
gift-release-deed.whoNeedsIt: Families transferring property between members without a sale, or releasing a share in jointly held property. Common after a family settlement, when one sibling wants to formally give up their share to another.
process: Relationship, property details and intent confirmed
Deed drafted and shared for review
Stamp duty coordination and registration assistance

power-of-attorney-drafting.title: Power of Attorney Drafting
power-of-attorney-drafting.summary: Drafting of General and Special Power of Attorney documents for property and related matters. We scope the exact powers granted carefully, so the document does what you intend and nothing more.
power-of-attorney-drafting.whoNeedsIt: Anyone authorising another person to act on their behalf for a property or legal matter. Especially relevant for NRIs or anyone unable to be physically present for a transaction or registration.
process: Purpose and scope of authority discussed
POA drafted to match the intended use
Execution and registration/notarisation guidance provided
documents: Details of the person being authorised

society-share-transfer.title: Housing Society Share Transfer
society-share-transfer.summary: Documentation support for transferring share certificates and flat ownership within a housing society. We prepare the transfer application in the format each society typically expects, to avoid back-and-forth.
society-share-transfer.whoNeedsIt: Flat owners transferring ownership after a sale, gift or family transfer within a co-operative society. Required whenever a flat changes hands, since the society's own records must be updated alongside the deed.
process: Transfer type and society requirements confirmed
Application and supporting documents prepared
Coordination with the society until the transfer is recorded

society-noc-membership.title: Society NOC & Membership Documentation
society-noc-membership.summary: Assistance in obtaining Society NOCs and completing membership documentation for Flat/Shop-related transactions, including preparation and scrutiny of requisite forms and supporting documents.
society-noc-membership.whoNeedsIt: New or existing members needing an NOC for sale, mortgage or other society-related purposes. Also useful if the society is delaying membership paperwork for a flat you've already purchased.
process: Purpose of the NOC/membership request confirmed
Application prepared per the society's format
Follow-up with the society/managing committee

sra-flat-transfer.title: SRA Flat Transfer Documentation
sra-flat-transfer.summary: Documentation assistance for transferring an SRA (Slum Rehabilitation Authority) flat, subject to eligibility. We review the specific SRA scheme's transfer rules before preparing any application.
sra-flat-transfer.whoNeedsIt: SRA flat owners transferring the flat to a family member or buyer, where permitted. Eligibility and lock-in conditions vary by scheme, so this is worth checking before assuming a transfer is possible.
process: Eligibility and transfer conditions reviewed
Application and supporting documents prepared
Coordination with the relevant authority until completion
documents: Copy of Annexure II issued or certified by the competent authority.
Copy of the SRA Allotment Letter / Ownership Letter.
Copy of the Society Share Certificate.
Aadhaar Card of the existing holder.
Aadhaar Card of the spouse, where applicable.
Photographs, allotment records or other records relating to the rehabilitation allotment, as applicable.
Copy of the possession letter or other possession record, if available.
Copy of the original rehabilitation agreement or other relevant allotment documents, if available.
Details of the SRA scheme, building, flat number and allotment date.
Details of any previous transfer, mortgage, litigation or restriction affecting the tenement.

mhada-flat-transfer.title: MHADA Flat Transfer Documentation
mhada-flat-transfer.summary: Assistance in MHADA flat transfer documentation, including family transfers, subject to applicable MHADA rules and eligibility requirements, comprising preparation and scrutiny of requisite documents, applications and undertakings.
mhada-flat-transfer.whoNeedsIt: MHADA flat or shop owners who wish to transfer their property to a family member or an eligible buyer. We assist in verifying ownership documents, applicable MHADA rules, eligibility criteria, and required approvals to ensure compliance with the relevant scheme regulations and lease conditions.
process: Transfer type and MHADA eligibility reviewed
Application and supporting documents prepared
Coordination with MHADA until the transfer is recorded

mmrda-property-documentation.title: MMRDA Property Documentation
mmrda-property-documentation.summary: Documentation assistance for properties involving MMRDA, subject to the applicable scheme's terms. We identify which MMRDA-specific approvals or NOCs your transaction actually needs.
mmrda-property-documentation.whoNeedsIt: Owners of MMRDA-linked properties needing transfer or related documentation support. Also useful if you're unsure which MMRDA scheme your property falls under.
process: Property and scheme details reviewed
Application and supporting documents prepared
Coordination with the relevant authority until completion

society-redevelopment-documentation.title: Society Redevelopment Documentation
society-redevelopment-documentation.summary: Legal documentation assistance for housing society redevelopment, including scrutiny and preparation of consents, resolutions, agreements and requisite approvals, with coordination among society members, Managing Committee and developers throughout the redevelopment process.
society-redevelopment-documentation.whoNeedsIt: We provide documentation and legal assistance to housing society members and managing committees throughout the redevelopment process, including the preparation and review of necessary documents, agreements, consents and approvals. We also assist individual members in understanding their legal rights, obligations and documentation requirements to ensure their interests are adequately protected during the redevelopment process.
process: Stage of the redevelopment and documentation gap reviewed
Required agreements/consents identified
Documentation prepared and coordinated with the relevant parties
documents: Original land title documents and previous conveyance deeds.
Latest Property Card / 7/12 Extract and relevant mutation entries.
City Survey records, CTS number, survey plan and land measurement records, as applicable.
Development Agreement or Lease Deed, if the land is leasehold or subject to development rights.
Existing building's sanctioned plan and available commencement and occupancy certificates.
Existing building's approved layout, completion records and other municipal approvals.
Property tax bills, land revenue receipts and other relevant dues records.
Documents relating to reservations, easements, mortgages, litigation or third-party claims affecting the land.
Deemed conveyance application and supporting records, if conveyance has not been completed.

legal-drafting-agreements-affidavits.title: Legal Drafting — Agreements, Affidavits & Notices
legal-drafting-agreements-affidavits.summary: Drafting assistance for agreements, affidavits, declarations, undertakings and legal notices. Each document is drafted to your specific facts, not from a generic template that may not hold up if challenged.
legal-drafting-agreements-affidavits.whoNeedsIt: Individuals and businesses needing a specific document drafted or reviewed. Also useful if you already have a draft and want a professional review before signing.
process: Purpose and key terms of the document discussed
Document drafted and shared for your review
Finalised after your inputs, with execution guidance
documents: Relevant background documents for the matter

public-notice-publication.title: Public Notice Publication
public-notice-publication.summary: Drafting and newspaper publication of public notices — for a lost title deed, a property sale objection window, a name change, or a similar legal requirement. We handle the drafting and coordinate publication in the required newspapers.
public-notice-publication.whoNeedsIt: Anyone needing to publish a notice for a lost document, an intended property sale, a change of name, or a similar legal requirement. Commonly needed before a property transaction closes, to invite objections within the notice period.
process: Purpose and required newspaper(s)/language confirmed
Notice drafted and shared for your approval
Published, with the tear sheet/proof of publication shared with you
documents: Details/proof relevant to the notice (e.g. FIR copy for a lost document, property papers for a sale notice)

nri-property-documentation.title: NRI Property Documentation
nri-property-documentation.summary: Legal documentation assistance for NRIs in property purchase, sale, transfer and Power of Attorney matters, including preparation and coordination of documents for remote execution, attestation and registration, subject to applicable laws and procedural requirements.
nri-property-documentation.whoNeedsIt: We provide legal documentation assistance to NRIs for managing property transactions in India remotely or through a duly authorised Power of Attorney holder, including registration and housing society formalities.
process: Requirement and location of the property confirmed
Documents drafted and shared for remote execution
Coordination with the POA holder/local representative as needed
documents: POA, if a representative will act locally

will-succession-documentation.title: Will & Succession Documentation
will-succession-documentation.summary: Drafting assistance for Wills, and documentation support for legal heir and succession matters. We also help coordinate the succession certificate or legal heir documentation needed after a death in the family.
will-succession-documentation.whoNeedsIt: Individuals wanting to draft a Will, or families handling succession documentation after a death in the family. Especially useful when multiple legal heirs are involved and consensus documentation is needed.
process: Assets and intended distribution discussed, or succession situation reviewed
Document(s) drafted and shared for review
Execution/registration guidance, or coordination for succession documentation
documents: Death certificate and family details, for succession matters

## Who we are

Growth Capital Services ("we", "us") is a loan advisory and facilitation firm. This policy explains what personal information we collect through this website, why, and the choices you have.

## What we collect

- Details you give us in forms: name, mobile number, email, city, the loan you need and the amount.
- Details you share while we work on your enquiry, such as income, employment and property information, and identity and address documents.
- Basic technical data when you visit: pages viewed, device and browser type, and the page you came from, collected through cookies and analytics tools.

## How we use it

- To contact you about your enquiry and assess which lenders may suit your profile.
- To prepare and submit your loan application to banks and NBFCs you ask us to approach.
- To send you updates about your file, and, where you agree, information about our services.
- To keep our records, meet legal obligations and improve this website.

## Who we share it with

We share your details with the banks, NBFCs and service providers (for example valuers, legal and technical agencies, and credit bureaus) needed to process your request, and only for that purpose. We do not sell your personal information.

## Credit reports

If you ask us to fetch a credit report, we do so only with your consent and use it only to advise you on your request.

## How long we keep it

We keep your information for as long as needed to serve you and to meet legal and record-keeping requirements, and then delete or anonymise it.

## Security

We use reasonable technical and organisational safeguards to protect your information. No system is completely secure, so please share sensitive documents only through the channels we give you.

## Your choices

You may ask to see, correct or delete the personal information we hold about you, or withdraw your consent to marketing, by contacting us below. We will respond within a reasonable time.

## Cookies

We use cookies and similar tools to make the site work and to understand how it is used. You can control cookies in your browser settings.

## About these terms

By using this website or contacting Growth Capital Services you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the site.

## What we do

We are a loan advisory and facilitation firm. We help you compare options across banks and NBFCs and support you through documentation and processing. We are not a bank or lender, and we do not sanction or disburse loans ourselves.

## No guarantee of approval

Whether a loan is approved, and its amount, rate and terms, is decided by the lender alone. Information on this site, including interest rates, calculators and eligibility tools, is indicative and is not an offer or commitment.

## Our fees

We do not charge customers an advisory fee for arranging a loan unless we tell you otherwise in writing before you proceed. We are paid by the lender on successful disbursal. Lenders may charge their own processing and other fees, which will be stated in their sanction documents.

## Your responsibilities

- Give us accurate and complete information and documents.
- Tell us promptly if anything changes.
- Do not misuse the site or attempt to disrupt it.

## Third-party content and links

Links to other websites are for convenience. We are not responsible for their content or practices.

## Limitation of liability

To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for any indirect or consequential loss arising from use of this site or from a lender's decision.

## Changes

We may update these terms from time to time. The version on this page applies from the date it is published.

## Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of India, and the courts at Mumbai have jurisdiction.

The information on this website is for general guidance only. It is not financial, legal, tax or investment advice, and you should consider your own circumstances before acting on it.

## We are not a lender

Growth Capital Services is not a bank, NBFC or lender. We facilitate loan applications with banks and NBFCs. All loans are subject to the lender's own eligibility criteria, credit assessment, documentation and approval.

## Rates, fees and calculators

Interest rates, processing fees, eligibility estimates and calculator results shown here are indicative and may change without notice. The final terms are those in the lender's sanction letter.

Bank and lender names and logos appear only to indicate the institutions we work with. They remain the property of their owners, and their appearance does not imply endorsement.

We try to keep the information current and accurate but do not guarantee that it is complete or error-free.
